rules.pattern: Purple-to-blue gradient
rules.why: The single most common AI default. If the palette is guessable from the category alone, it is a training reflex, not a decision.

rules.pattern: Purple / magenta neon glow, cyan-on-dark, dark mode with glowing accents as the default
rules.why: Glow is used to hide weak hierarchy. Colour must be used in whole fields with roles, not as a wash.

rules.pattern: Gradient text
rules.why: Reads as a generator default and hurts legibility. Use solid colour text only.

rules.pattern: Glowing blobs / glassmorphism / glassy cards by default
rules.why: Decoration with no job. Every element must earn its place.

rules.pattern: Pure black #000 / pure white #fff
rules.why: Untinted extremes look unconsidered. Tint neutrals toward the brand hue.

rules.pattern: Grey text on a coloured background
rules.why: Washes out. Use a shade of the background colour for text on colour.

rules.pattern: Second-wave default clusters: warm-cream + high-contrast serif + terracotta; near-black + acid-green/vermilion; broadsheet hairline-rules layout used as a reflex
rules.why: These replaced the purple gradient as the new defaults. A direction needs a reason tied to the subject, not a swap of one default for another.

rules.pattern: Inter / Roboto / Arial / Open Sans / system defaults used for everything with no stated reason
rules.why: A font needs a stated role-based reason. Defaults signal no decision was made.

rules.pattern: Replacement defaults used the same way: DM Sans, Outfit, Plus Jakarta, Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, Fraunces, Playfair, Lora
rules.why: Swapping one default for another is still a default. Choose a pairing for the subject and say why.

rules.pattern: Italic headings as a decorative default
rules.why: Italics are emphasis, not a personality.

rules.pattern: One coloured / accented word inside a headline
rules.why: A generator tic. If one word needs colour to be interesting, the headline is weak.

rules.pattern: Centred hero + 2 buttons + 3 identical feature cards (the 'SaaS card kit')
rules.why: Identical rounded cards, one radius everywhere, one soft grey shadow, decorative gradient washes. Design from the subject instead.

rules.pattern: Identical-card feature grids; hero-metric layouts; sparkline decorations
rules.why: Even, timid composition. Vary section compositions and commit to a grid for a reason.

rules.pattern: Cards inside cards; floating card cascades with no purpose; fake chatbot popups; fake browser frames; coloured left-border cards
rules.why: Frames around frames add noise, not meaning.

rules.pattern: ALL-CAPS eyebrow above every heading; tracked-capital labels everywhere
rules.why: Ration ornaments: at most 1 eyebrow per 3 sections. Everything equally loud means nothing is loud.

rules.pattern: An arrow on every button; numbered markers (01, 02, 03) when the content is not a sequence; a large icon with rounded corners above every heading
rules.why: Ornament rationing. Motion and icons must communicate state or meaning.

rules.pattern: Generic pill buttons everywhere; h-screen hero that overflows on mobile
rules.why: The hero must fit its screen with CTAs visible without scrolling. Use min-h-100dvh, not h-screen.

rules.pattern: A · B · C meta strings; labels built with spaced em dashes; monospace data labels as decoration
rules.why: Filler chrome that imitates editorial design without doing its work.

rules.pattern: Placeholder lorem ipsum in a delivered design
rules.why: Nothing is invented. Real copy in the user's words, or a marked proof gap.

rules.pattern: Invented stats, testimonials or logos — e.g. 'Trusted by 10,000+ teams'
rules.why: Every number must trace to intake or research. Unsupported claims become questions, not copy.

rules.pattern: Email sign-up at the end of every page; a form that says 'thanks' without sending anything
rules.why: Fake forms are a trust tell. A form destination must be real.

rules.pattern: A page of empty frames, or nothing but photographs, with no real content
rules.why: Strip the ornaments: if the page reads thin, add substance, not decoration.

rules.pattern: "It's not X, it's Y" / "not only X but Y" negative parallelisms
rules.why: Formulaic AI sentence shape. Say what it is, directly.

rules.pattern: Forced rule of three (three abstract nouns); synonym cycling
rules.why: Padding. Every sentence must carry a claim, example, number, constraint or image.

rules.pattern: Em-dash overuse (more than 1 per passage as a rule of thumb)
rules.why: A cluster tell. One deliberate dash is fine; a dash in every sentence is a fingerprint.

rules.pattern: "Serves as / stands as / boasts" instead of is/has; '-ing' analysis phrases (showcasing, fostering, underscoring)
rules.why: Inflated, actorless language. Use active voice with a real human subject.

rules.pattern: Significance inflation: pivotal, testament, landscape, seamless, delve
rules.why: Words that claim importance instead of demonstrating it.

rules.pattern: Vague attribution: 'experts believe', 'studies show' with no study named
rules.why: Evidence-bound writing: name the source or cut the claim.

rules.pattern: Chatbot leftovers: 'Certainly!', 'As an AI…', drafting notes, summary endings that repeat the point
rules.why: The artefact must not contain the process that made it.

rules.pattern: Bold mini-heading lists ('**Performance:** Performance has…'); title-case everything; decorative emoji
rules.why: Formatting used as a substitute for structure and claims.

rules.pattern: Animating everything; motion used to hide weak information architecture
rules.why: Motion must communicate state, hierarchy or continuity — trigger, move, settle — and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.pattern: Gratuitous blobs, fake 3D, neon overload
rules.why: Decoration that competes with the content.

rules.pattern: Mermaid-default diagrams; shadows in diagrams
rules.why: Editorial diagrams: one accent, 1px hairlines, 4px grid, no shadows.

reminder: Take principles, not pictures. Record 1 primary + at most 1 secondary reference, each for a NAMED dimension, and list what was intentionally NOT copied.
source_note: Restated in our own words from the research report §1.1, which synthesises Hallmark, Impeccable, Taste-Skill, Anthropic frontend-design, stop-slop, blader/humanizer, unslop, slopbeth and diagram-design. Rule IDs are stable so other tools can cite them.
two_order_test: If the look is guessable from the category alone ('AI tool = dark + purple', 'finance = navy + serif'), it is a training reflex — rework. If it is guessable from category + the obvious anti-reference, rework again.
